note: A METER for the github-code-quality analyzer, not a gate. Records findings and the adjudicated true-positive / false-positive split so the keep-or-disable decision becomes answerable with data. Resolution state is RECORDED but is never an input to the split: 141 of the 269 enumerated threads were resolved by the analyzer itself (exactly the 141 marked isOutdated), so 'resolved' means the diff moved under it, not that the finding was real. DISCREPANCY ON RECORD: the adjudication session of 2026-08-24 was described as 18 findings (16 false / 2 real), but the itemisation names 4 + 10 + 1 false and 2 real, and the API census finds exactly 17 analyzer threads across those five files. 17 is what is seeded (15 false-positive, 2 true-positive); the 18th is not reproducible from the API and is deliberately NOT invented to make the brief's arithmetic close.

census.method: GET /repos/Lucent-Financial-Group/Zeta/pulls/comments (repo-wide review comments, sort=created&direction=desc) paginated to exhaustion — the endpoint ran out at page 270 of 100, i.e. 26,975 review comments total, and pages 233-270 contained zero analyzer comments. 269 analyzer comments found. Each hosting PR was then re-queried via GraphQL reviewThreads for isResolved / isOutdated / resolvedBy; that pass independently returned 269 threads, matching the REST count exactly. The census is COMPLETE for this endpoint, not a sample.
knownGaps: Review comments on DELETED pull requests are unreachable via this endpoint; none were observed but their absence cannot be proven from here.
Findings the analyzer reported as check-run annotations rather than as review threads are out of scope — this census covers review threads only.
Analyzer comments that a maintainer deleted outright leave no trace in the API and are therefore uncountable.
The window opens 2026-04-29 because that is the analyzer's FIRST comment in a fully-enumerated history, not because enumeration stopped there.

entries.evidenceNote: Pure bigint arithmetic on `SEED + 1n + off` — no index access anywhere on the flagged lines. Disproved by planting the real defect (an unguarded indexed read) and watching `tsc` catch it at that exact line under `strict` + `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`; the analyzer's finding survived unchanged.
